prompt.title: THE LAST BARGAIN
lines: The Thing in the Chapel is down, and for the first time in years the bell hangs silent — waiting.
The bargain is still his to hold. Or his to break.
What does the Hollow King do?

choices.label: Break the bell
choices.hint: End the bargain. End everything it holds — himself included.

choices.label: Keep the vigil
choices.hint: Swallow the curse whole and stand watch over it. Forever.

bell.title: The Bell Broken
bell.epitaph: the bell is silent. the dead sleep.
lines: The bell comes down with a sound like a held breath ending. The dead in the courtyard sway once — and lie down, all of them, gently, like a field going to sleep.
The king goes with them. He knew he would. Whatever held him upright was part of the bargain too.
They bury him in the churchyard with the people he doomed and saved. Maud digs it herself. "Proper depth," she says. "He's earned the full six."
The vale keeps the vigil now only out of habit. Some nights, the survivors still sit up by the fire — and nothing comes, and that is everything.

vigil.title: The Vigil Kept
vigil.epitaph: the king keeps the vigil. the nights are his.
lines: He does not break the bell. He swallows it — bargain, curse, and all — and sits back down on the throne of Castle Vane to hold it shut from the inside.
The dead still rise, some nights. But they rise CONFUSED now, leaderless, thin — and the vale knows how to meet them.
Travelers say a light burns in the castle's highest window, every night, all night. It has not gone out in living memory.
"He bought the night," Wren says at the fire, to anyone new. "Somebody's got to keep the receipt."
